newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyu says to post 27.7 bln yen loss in US unit.
newsitem.headline: Tokyu says to post 27.7 bln yen loss in US unit.

text.p: Tokyu Corp said on Tuesday that it would post an extraordinary loss of 27.7 billion yen in securities holdings in its U.S. subsidiary in 1996/97.

The subsidiary, wholly owned by Tokyu, has been operating resort hotels and developing real estate in Hawaii since 1972, but its earnings fell sharply amid the deterioration of the real-estate market in late 1980s, Tokyu said in a statement.
It said the subsidiary's problems resulted in Tokyu sustaining the loss in the securities it held in the company.

However, the company said it would maintain its forecast of 6.3 billion yen in parent net profit for the year ending on March 31. The company said that the extraordinary loss would be offset by sales of part of its stockholdings and property.

The company concurrently revised downward its forecast of parent sales in 1996/97 to 292 billion yen from 299 billion yen, but revised upward the forecast of parent current profit to 30 billion yen from 22 billion yen.
